![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13997987/assets/8e85666a72dde1ebbe24ff3d8dbb1404f010e81d9406aec790be11416b705f00.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
feedback.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(3,-6).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=p{t}^{2},\,y=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(3,-6),$ we can substitute $x=3$ and $y=-6$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}3=p{t}^{2} \\ -6=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-6 & =2pt \\ -3 & =pt \\ t & =-\frac{3}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =p{(-\frac{3}{p})}^{2} \\ 3 & =p\cdot \frac{9}{{p}^{2}} \\ 3 & =\frac{9}{p} \\ p & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=(3){t}^{2},\,y=2(3)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=3{t}^{2},\,y=6t.
$$
